instructions: If your steak isn't already shaved, put it in the freezer for 30 minutes first. It's much easier to slice thin when it's firm.
Slice the 1.5 lb steak across the grain as thin as you can, trimming off any big pieces of fat. Dice the onion.
Set out 2 tbsp butter to soften. Press or finely mince the garlic clove and mash it into the butter with a fork.
Slice the 4 hoagie rolls about three quarters of the way through so they open like a book. Spread the garlic butter over the cut sides.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium. Lay the rolls in cut side down and toast them for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden. Set them aside.
Add 1 tbsp oil to the same pan, still on medium. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook, stirring now and then, for 8 to 10 minutes, until it's soft and golden brown. Tip it into a bowl.
Turn the heat up to high and add the last 1 tbsp oil. Spread the steak out in an even layer and leave it alone for 2 minutes, until the underside is browned.

Turn the steak over and sprinkle it with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper. Cook it for 1 to 2 minutes, breaking it up with your spatula, until there's no pink left. Stir the onion back in.
Taste a piece of the beef, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Split the beef into 4 piles in the pan and lay the 8 slices of provolone over them, 2 on each pile. Turn off the heat and leave it for 1 to 2 minutes, until the cheese melts.

Spread the 3 tbsp mayonnaise thinly over the toasted sides of the rolls. Lay a roll open over one pile, slide your spatula under the beef and flip it all into the roll. Do the same with the other three.
method_notes: Both read versions slice ribeye very thin (Once Upon a Chef freezes it for 35 to 45 minutes first, and also allows sirloin), brown the onion separately, sear the steak hard over high heat and melt the cheese over the beef in the pan before it goes into toasted rolls. Natasha's Kitchen toasts the rolls in garlic butter, uses mild provolone and spreads the rolls with mayo. Once Upon a Chef adds a bell pepper and a splash of cider vinegar to the onions, sears in two batches and melts American cheese through the meat before shingling provolone on top. This follows Natasha's method but uses Once Upon a Chef's 1.5 lb of steak for four, since Natasha's 1 lb makes a light sandwich.
